original_question: Determine whether there exist discrete random-tree models that look superficially different from the critical beta-splitting model but have the same continuum limit CTCS(infinity), in the sense of converging to the same exchangeable-partition-based infinite random tree object.
target_in_paper: Section 7.3, Open Problem 15: "Are there superficially different discrete models whose limit is the same CTCS(∞)?" The nearby context explains that CTCS(∞) is the paper’s infinite limit object for the consistent family (CTCS(n)) and that the authors view subordinator approximation (4) as the likely structural reason such a phenomenon might occur. ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2303/2303.02529v2.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already gets the core target right: it asks for existence of other discrete models, insists they be only superficially different from the critical beta-splitting model, and identifies the relevant notion of sameness as having the same limit object CTCS(∞), understood through the paper’s exchangeable-partition formalization rather than through a purely finite-n comparison. ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2303/2303.02529v2.pdf))
missing_details: The paper states this as an open problem, specifically Open Problem 15 in Section 7.3, not as a theorem or named conjecture. ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2303/2303.02529v2.pdf))

To make the question stand-alone, you should identify the reference model: the critical beta-splitting model has split probabilities q(m,i)=m/[2 h_{m-1} i(m-i)] for 1≤i≤m−1, with h_{m-1}=∑_{j=1}^{m-1}1/j, and its associated continuous-time version CTCS(n) splits a size-m clade at rate h_{m-1}. ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2303/2303.02529v2.pdf))

The phrase "same continuum limit" needs tightening, because the paper explicitly says CTCS(∞) is formalized via exchangeable partitions and is less naturally phrased as a random element of a standard metric-space topology. So the question should say "same limit object CTCS(∞)" or explicitly refer to the same exchangeable partition process Π(t), not an unspecified continuum-limit topology. ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2303/2303.02529v2.pdf))

The paper’s formalization of CTCS(∞) comes from the consistency theorem: deleting leaf n+1 and pruning CTCS(n+1) yields CTCS(n), which lets one define a consistent growth process and then a partition Π(t) of N at each height t. That structure is part of what "same CTCS(∞)" means. ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2303/2303.02529v2.pdf))

The exchangeable-partition details are implicit in your draft but should be made explicit: Π(t) partitions N into clades at height t, and Theorem 10 describes this partition through asymptotic clade frequencies Pt,ℓ via Kingman’s paintbox. ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2303/2303.02529v2.pdf))

The nearby heuristic the authors actually attach to the problem is that the key feature of the model seems to be the subordinator approximation log X_t^(n)≈log n−Y_t while Y_t<log n; this is the specific mechanism they suggest might recur in some other model. ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2303/2303.02529v2.pdf))

No ambient ring, field, operator, homogeneity, degree, nilpotency, or "for all sufficiently large m" clause is relevant here; this is a probabilistic random-tree question, so those items are not missing data but inapplicable categories. ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2303/2303.02529v2.pdf))
refined_question: Let CTCS(∞) denote the infinite limit object associated with the critical beta-splitting model, where a size-m clade splits with probabilities q(m,i)=m/[2 h_{m-1} i(m-i)] for 1≤i≤m−1 and, in the continuous-time embedding CTCS(n), at rate h_{m-1}; equivalently, CTCS(∞) is the exchangeable partition-valued limit obtained from the consistent family (CTCS(n)) by cutting at each height t≥0. Are there discrete models that are superficially different from this critical beta-splitting model but whose limit object is nevertheless the same CTCS(∞) in distribution? ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2303/2303.02529v2.pdf))
justification: The draft is targeting Open Problem 15 almost verbatim, not a broader neighboring problem. The exact paper-language is about the existence of superficially different discrete models with the same limit CTCS(∞), and the surrounding discussion in Section 7.3 ties this to comparison with the Brownian CRT and to the authors’ heuristic that subordinator approximation (4) is the decisive structural feature. To make the question fully stand-alone and paper-faithful, one must define the reference critical beta-splitting model, note that CTCS(∞) is obtained from the consistency theorem for CTCS(n), and clarify that the paper formalizes CTCS(∞) through the exchangeable partition process Π(t), not via a specified metric-space convergence notion. Because the paper does not state a separate numbered equivalence for Open Problem 15 itself, I have not supplied an alternate formulation beyond this sharpened stand-alone version. ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2303/2303.02529v2.pdf))
